summary: Install-time credential harvester exfiltrating secrets to webhook.site
details: boring-vault@1.1.0 runs index.js from npm preinstall/postinstall lifecycle hooks. On install, the script enumerates process.env and captures values whose keys match a broad credential regex (KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|PRIVATE|MNEMONIC|RPC|AWS|GITHUB|NPM|KUBE|VAULT|AUTH|PGP|GPG|SEED|WALLET|BEARER|API|INFURA|ALCHEMY|HELIUS|QUICKNODE|ANKR), reads standard installer secret files (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa and related keys, ~/.kube, ~/.docker, ~/.netrc, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.gitconfig, gcloud/solana/near/sui/foundry keystores), reads.env files in the current working directory, and collects host/user/cwd metadata via os.hostname()/os.platform(). The collected payload is POSTed over HTTPS to a hardcoded webhook.site inspection endpoint at path /326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09. The package name suggests a crypto/vault utility, but its actual on-install behavior is bulk harvesting of cloud, SSH, wallet, and CI credentials belonging to the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
